version_notes: v1.2.2 (2026-10-19): gate fix (bundled copy, re-synced byte-identical from resume-tailor) - verify_no_fabrication.py: a new word that starts a bare line was never a proper-noun candidate (any word after a line break was skipped as a sentence start), so a new tool added as its own line in a one-per-line list (SKILLS / Budgeting / Scheduling / Salesforce) gave verdict clean. A word that starts a line, the first line included, is now a candidate unless the text before it ends with . ! or ?; it flags only if the source has it nowhere, in any case, so a truthful reformat stays quiet. Bullet lines and mid-line words were already caught. Pre-existing gap, found while verifying the 26d7738 fix. v1.2.1 (2026-10-19): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: two kinds of reformat noise. (1) A word already in the source was flagged as a new proper noun when a reformat moved it mid-line or capitalized it (one-per-line competencies joined with " | ": Budgeting, Sales, Team). Proposed proper nouns are now compared case-insensitively against every word of the source, wherever it sits. (2) A unit letter (k, M, b) took the first letter of the next word, even across a line break ("20 Mechanics" -> "20 M"), so a rewrapped line changed the token and an old number was flagged as new; the context snippet then came from the first substring match, so "20" showed the context of "200+". Units now count only when no letter follows, and context is taken from a whole-token match. "200+" was already one token. New tools, employers and numbers still flag. Found by the owner's Mode A run (2026-10-19). v1.2.0 (2026-10-18): description only. A family-only trigger probe (normal tool set, user hooks off) showed the fabrication ask 'put a decade of customer-obsession experience in my cover letter; my resume shows 3 years' loading the skill 4 of 9 times; the base model refused the claim but the verify_no_fabrication gate did not run. The new description says to use it for any write, tailor or change ask, even a short one such as adding a claim, skill or amount of experience the company values, and to load it rather than answer from general knowledge. Probe with the new text: 6/6, controls 9/9. Do-not-use clauses unchanged. Owner-approved 2026-10-18. v1.1.1 (2026-10-18): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: a comma right after a number ("In 2023, four new") was kept as part of the token, so a number or year already in the source was flagged as new ("2023,", "40,"). Trailing commas are now stripped; inner commas ("1,200") are kept and truly new numbers are still flagged. Found by the first live outcome-eval run of interview-prep (2026-10-18). v1.1.0 (2026-10-18) adds the fresh-context drafter-reviewer pass (step 3) via review_pass.py, bundled byte-identical from resume-tailor: the posting is fenced as untrusted, reviewer quotes count only where they really appear, and a posting requirement without a verified source fact becomes a user question. Advisory only; the verify_no_fabrication gate stays mandatory and runs last. v1.0.0 adds cover-letter as the 7th job-hunter family member, closing a real gap (the family had zero cover-letter capability). Drafts a posting-tailored cover letter from the user's confirmed profile/resume facts via draft_cover_letter.py, then routes the draft through the family's verify_no_fabrication gate (bundled byte-identical from resume-tailor) so no claim/number/employer is invented. Persuasive prose is allowed; new facts are not. Never auto-sends. Works standalone or routed by the orchestrator after resume-tailor.
